stepNotes.1: Single-file LifecycleHooks namespace mapping 6 event names to shell packs from builtin/project-file/config; execution is spawn(shell:true) at lifecycle.ts:241 with args via env (capped 32KiB) + stdin.
stepNotes.2: Dominant boundary is repository-controlled .ax-code/hooks.json leading to RCE via shell:true; defense is loadProjectHooks early-return on ProjectConfigTrust.enabled() (env-only AX_CODE_TRUST_PROJECT_CONFIG); secondary concerns are capture truncation, EPIPE suppression, and process-group SIGKILL on timeout.
stepNotes.3: Trust gate fires before fs.readFile (lifecycle.ts:186); Zod safeParse rejects malformed entries to []; blockOnFailure only vetoes PreToolUse/UserPromptSubmit; settled flag prevents double-resolve of exit promise; hooks run sequentially with block-break.
stepNotes.4: Explicit bounds: MAX_CONCURRENT_HOOKS=4 semaphore, MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES=1MiB truncation, HOOK_TIMEOUT_MS=30s, MAX_COMPAT_ENV_BYTES=32KiB; no unbounded maps; selectHooks is O(hooks) over a .max(100) schema cap.
stepNotes.5: Trust policy correctly externalized to ProjectConfigTrust (env-only) so this module only consumes a boolean; mild smell is inline node -e scripts in builtin packs; clean @/util/@/config/@/project/@/global imports.
stepNotes.6: globalHooksDir() exported but no reader in this file (possibly unwired stub); child.stdin.on(error,()=>undefined) is a documented EPIPE suppression not a silent-error defect; catch{return []} is deliberate invalid-config policy behind the trust gate.
